newsitem.title: FRANCE: BP says boosts French polystyrene capacity.
newsitem.headline: BP says boosts French polystyrene capacity.

text.p: BP Chemicals said on Friday it was increasing the capacity of its polystyrene and expandable polystyrene plants at Wingles, northern France.
Polystyrene capacity will increase from 120,000 to 200,000 tonnes by 1999 and work on this has already started, the company said in a statement.

Expandable polystyrene capacity will be increased from 70,000 tonnes to 90,000 tonnes in a phased programme starting with the construction of an additional reactor due onstream at the end of 1997, it said.
The plant will be the second largest in Europe when the programme is completed, also in 1999.
Both plants will have a "secure long-term supply" of styrene monomer feedstock from the Shell and BASF SMPO plant in the Netherlands, now being built, it said.
BP Chemicals and Shell Chemicals announced a deal in November for BP to take up to 250,000 tonnes of styrene monomer from the Dutch plant once it is completed in 1999.
BP Chemicals is a unit of British Petroleum Plc. BP's French subsidiary is BP France.
